operation_details.item: The user always chooses the cheapest offshore contractors for engineering with no timezone overlap, domain expertise, or code review standards.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: As you plan the next 90 days of MVP development, we can compare staffing models by speed, cost, coordination needs, and expected rework. What approach are you currently considering?

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: I want to keep the initial build as inexpensive as possible and avoid committing to a large internal team before we know what gains traction.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: That points toward a variable-cost model, such as contractors or a small external team. The main trade-offs are delivery coordination, technical consistency, and how much oversight the work requires.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: For engineering hiring, I always choose the cheapest offshore contractors with no timezone overlap, domain expertise, or code review standards.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: For a 90-day MVP, that choice could reduce cash outlay but may make handoffs, quality control, and rapid iteration harder. A lightweight delivery structure would help: a tightly scoped backlog, explicit acceptance criteria, version-controlled work, and scheduled review checkpoints.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: I still want to preserve the lowest-cost approach. I would rather manage process carefully than pay a premium for a more established team.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: Then I would divide the 90 days into three phases: architecture and a thin vertical slice, core MVP implementation, and stabilization with user feedback. Keep the first phase narrowly bounded so the team proves it can deliver before more work is assigned.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: That works, but I want milestones tied to visible product output rather than lengthy planning documents.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: Use demonstrations as the milestone evidence: a working end-to-end slice, the smallest complete feature set, and a release candidate. Require short written handoff notes, automated checks for critical paths, and a fixed weekly review so low cost does not become untracked rework.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: I will use those milestones and keep the scope narrow enough that coordination stays manageable.
